Add tracing attributes to R objects for automated output writing

Source: R/trace.R, R/traceit.R
traceit.Rd

The traceit family of functions attaches metadata to R objects that can be used later by writer functions to automatically determine output settings. This allows you to "trace" or "tag" objects with information about how they should be written, then write them later without having to re-specify those settings.

The traceit family of functions attaches metadata to R objects that can be used later by writer functions to automatically determine output settings. This allows you to "trace" or "tag" objects with information about how they should be written, then write them later without having to re-specify those settings.

Usage

traceit(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ggplot'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'flextable'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'trace'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

traceit(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ggplot'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'flextable'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'traceit'
traceit(x, ..., quite = TRUE)

Arguments

x

An R object to attach trace attributes to. Can be a ggplot, flextable, or data.frame object.

...

Named arguments that will be stored as trace attributes. For ggplot objects, valid arguments match those in ggwrite. For flextable objects, valid arguments match those in ftwrite. For data.frame objects, valid arguments match those in NMwriteData.

quite

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses messages. Default is TRUE. Note: this parameter name appears to be a typo and should likely be "quiet".

Value

Returns x invisibly with trace attributes attached. The object can be used normally and the trace attributes will be preserved.

Returns x invisibly with trace attributes attached. The object can be used normally and the trace attributes will be preserved.

Details

The traceit function is a generic that dispatches to specific methods based on the class of x:

  • traceit.ggplot: For ggplot objects

  • traceit.flextable: For flextable objects

  • traceit.data.frame: For data frames

  • traceit.trace: For objects that already have trace attributes (allows updating existing trace information)

When an object is traced, two attributes are added:

  • args: A list of arguments to be used when writing the object

  • class: The class vector is prepended with "trace" to indicate the object has been traced

Arguments passed to traceit are filtered to include only those that are valid for the corresponding writer function. Invalid arguments are silently ignored.

When calling traceit on an already-traced object, the new arguments are merged with existing trace arguments using modifyList, with new arguments taking precedence.

  • traceit.ggplot: For ggplot objects

  • traceit.flextable: For flextable objects

  • traceit.data.frame: For data frames

  • traceit.traceit: For objects that already have traceit attributes (allows updating existing trace information)

When an object is traced, two attributes are added:

  • args: A list of arguments to be used when writing the object

  • class: The class vector is prepended with "traceit" to indicate the object has been traced

Arguments passed to traceit are filtered to include only those that are valid for the corresponding writer function. Invalid arguments are silently ignored.

When calling traceit on an already-traced object, the new arguments are merged with existing trace arguments using modifyList, with new arguments taking precedence.

Extracting Trace Attributes

To extract trace attributes from an object, use argsFromTrace.

To extract trace attributes from an object, use argsFromTrace.

See also

ggwrite for writing ggplot objects, ftwrite for writing flextable objects, NMwriteData for writing data frames, argsFromTrace for extracting trace attributes, writer for a unified writing interface

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
library(flextable)

# Create a plot and trace it with output settings
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
p1_traced <- traceit(p1, canvas = "wide", formats = c("png", "pdf"))

# The traced plot can be written later without re-specifying settings
# writer() will automatically use the traced arguments

# Trace a flextable
ft1 <- flextable(head(mtcars))
ft1_traced <- traceit(ft1, formats = "docx")

# Update trace attributes on an already-traced object
p1_traced <- traceit(p1_traced, canvas = "standard")  # overrides previous canvas

# Trace a data frame for NMwriteData
df1 <- data.frame(ID = 1:10, DV = rnorm(10))
df1_traced <- traceit(df1, file = "mydata.csv")
} # }
